subject: SpectraOps renewal - bakeoff & uplift timeline
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@spectraops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@spectraops.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SpectraOps renewal - request for benchmark window

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick chat today. As we discussed, SpectraOps is coming up on our renewal (Apr 15) and the engineering team will be running a short bakeoff with two other vendors the week of Mar 13. Before we commit to a vendor we need:

- A short (3–5 day) benchmark window that mirrors our production mix (primarily chat + embedding serving, ~120k tokens/day).
- A test harness to run our 95th percentile latency checks and a KV cache scenario.
- A clear cost estimate for committed capacity at 500k tokens/day vs burst.

Can Redwood provide the harness and a short win plan (timing + what you need from us)? Priya and I will own scheduling on our side. We really like Redwood’s runtime but need to see head-to-head latency and cost delta.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
SpectraOps

Subject: Re: SpectraOps renewal - request for benchmark window

Alex —

Thanks for the note and for sharing the baseline. We can definitely run a 3–5 day bakeoff. Proposed next steps:

1) Redwood provides a harness and ingest instructions by Wed (Mar 1).
2) SpectraOps runs initial baseline load (you have the CSV) and we replicate traffic in our sandbox cluster the week of Mar 13.
3) We run two scenario sets: low-latency (p95 goal 250ms) and heavy-kv (stateful chat with cache warm).
4) Side-by-side cost model for committed vs burst (we’ll show unit cost per 1k tokens at 500k/day).

To make this productive, could you confirm whether the test data includes long context sessions (>2k tokens) and whether you need private VPC access for the run?

I’ve looped in Monica (CS lead) and Karthik (solutions). We’ll draft a straightforward mutual action plan and a single-page tech plan.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: SpectraOps renewal - internal bakeoff plan and proposed save package

Folks —

Forwarding the SpectraOps thread. They’re doing a 3rd-party bakeoff week of Mar 14 and they’ve shared a baseline with 20% long-context sessions. We need a practical save plan that wins on latency and shows a compelling committed-capacity price. My suggested approach:

- Technical: run two test profiles (latency focused p95 target 250ms; kv-heavy long-context). Use our GPU-optimized kernels + prefix caching to show p95 improvements. Provide a short metrics dashboard during the run.
- Commercial: offer a 12-month committed uplift at a blended unit rate that is ~18% below their current committed pricing for the first 6 months, with a one-time onboarding credit of $25k and a guaranteed regional failover window.
- SLA/ops: 99.9% API uptime SLA for dedicated capacity, 4-hour priority escalation during the bakeoff and first 60 days post-renewal.

Ask: Monica / Karthik — can you run the cost model and confirm we can deliver the $25k onboarding credit + blended pricing while keeping margin? Laura — need legal to pre-draft a short term-sheet (non-binding) we can send after the bakeoff if results look good.

Timing is tight; Alex wants the harness by Mar 1 and the run on the 14th. If we can commit today to the commercial outline I’ll send a one-pager to the customer with the technical plan and a DocuSign term sheet.

Thanks,
Marcus

Alex / Priya —

Great to run through the harness today. Summary and proposed next steps below (short version):

What we ran
- 4-day bakeoff run (Mar 14–17) across two profiles: low-latency p95 and kv-heavy long-context. We used your baseline dataset and replicated session distribution.
- Observed p95 latency: Redwood 240ms (latency profile) vs Competitor A 370ms; cost delta at 500k tokens/day: Redwood unit cost ~0.84/1k tokens committed vs competitor ~0.95/1k tokens.

Save package (one-pager attached)
- 12-month committed uplift to 500k tokens/day at blended unit rate 0.84/1k tokens for first 6 months, then 0.92/1k thereafter.
- $25,000 onboarding credit applied to first invoice.
- 99.9% API uptime SLA, priority escalation (4h) during the first 60 days.
- Post-bakeoff health check at 30 days and an automated fallback policy if any key SLA breaches are detected.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf, docusign-term-sheet-789.pdf

If that commercial outline sounds good, we’ll kick a short DocuSign and follow with an operational onboarding plan. If you want a narrower pilot (30d smaller commit) we can do that too but it will change the unit economics.

Next steps:
- Alex: confirm internal decision timeline (you mentioned renew by Apr 15).
- Priya: approval to proceed to DocuSign if numbers are acceptable.
- Monica/Karthik: I’ll send the cost model and final numbers by EOD tomorrow per your ask.

Thanks — really enjoyed the run and the team was great to work with.

Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
